quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It protects your whole face, not just your eyes.
It does not protect your face as well as goggles do.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your whole face, not just your eyes.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good replacement for either.

questions.question: Your tire goes flat while riding. What should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake gently on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake gently on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold both handlebars firmly. Ease off the throttle and keep the motorcycle straight. Slowly use the brake on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power does the front brake provide?

options.text: It should only be used when the road is wet.
It is the only brake you should use.

questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders be positioned in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can watch them from behind.

questions.question: What is the best way to increase your visibility while riding?

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Keep your headlight on all the time.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on all the time.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright and reflective clothes, keep your headlight on at all times, and change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: What does it mean when a rider extends their left arm straight out?

options.text: The rider is going to turn left.
The rider is about to stop.
The rider is going to turn right.
The rider is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider is going to turn left.
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals instead of turn signals to show turns or stops. When the left arm is extended straight out, it means the rider is turning left or changing lanes to the left.

questions.question: What color is a warning sign?

options.text: Yellow with black letters or symbols.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black letters or symbols.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake pedal on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The rear brake is controlled by a pedal near the right footrest.

questions.question: How can you stop other drivers from sharing your lane?

options.text: By giving dirty looks to other drivers.
By riding in the center of the lane.
By riding in the left portion of the lane.
By riding in a zigzag pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: By riding in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane so there is no large space on either side of your motorcycle. When there is less space, other drivers will be less likely to try to share the lane.

questions.question: How should you position yourself so the car ahead can see you in their mirror?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: When following a car, ride in the center of your lane. This places you directly in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: Which formation keeps riders in a group closest together?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets a group stay close together while giving each rider enough space. Single-file is better for curves, turns, and entering or leaving highways.

questions.question: The body removes about one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining in the system.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle, they should:
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider waits until the first rider safely returns to the original lane before passing.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Apply both brakes together to stop quickly.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Change your lane position as conditions change.
Go faster than usual to reach your destination sooner.
Always use your low beam headlight for better vision.
Follow closely behind the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position as conditions change.
questions.explanation: Stay flexible with your lane position, especially at night. Use safe riding strategies when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Speed up to create distance between you and them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Get the tailgater in front of you. If safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make things worse by letting them tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Near possible hazards like intersections, position your hands ready on the clutch and both brakes. This cuts down your response time if danger appears.

questions.question: When braking, use:

options.text: Either the front or rear brake, not both.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Sit as far back on the bike as possible.

questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean when the operator leans. They should sit forward without crowding the operator and hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, ride:

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: When should you keep a larger distance between you and other vehicles?

options.text: When it is colder than usual.
When you are following other motorcycles.

questions.explanation: A two-second distance is normally safe. Increase this distance when conditions make it harder to stop, such as on wet or icy roads.

questions.question: What should you NOT check during a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn. You do not need to check reflectors during a pre-ride inspection.

questions.question: When does alcohol start to affect your ability to ride safely?
questions.explanation: Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol. Your riding ability starts to worsen well before you reach the legal limit.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield cannot replace a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: Which type of sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. You must follow all rules shown on these signs.
